subject: Geofence pool commitment & node mapping proposal
messages:
From: Jules Martin <jules@edgelabs.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Cho <sarah@procureco.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pools by geofence - initial ask

Hiro,

Thanks again for taking this. We ran the traffic forecasts and want to propose committing to dedicated geofence-scoped pools in three regions: US (west coast), EU (Frankfurt), APAC (Singapore). High-level numbers below — these are our internal expected sustained requirements over the next 12 months: 

- Models: mixture of fine-tuned Transformer family (heavy KV cache). Peak tokens/day ~ 45M, steady-state ~ 18M tokens/day.
- Concurrency target: 120 concurrent sessions across regions; p95 latency target <= 220ms for text-gen.
- Preferred instances: A100S-80GB equivalent (for KV + long context).
- Desired reserve: ability to burst +30% for 4 hours/day during marketing spikes.
- Start window: committed capacity available by 2026-10-15.

We need a proposal that ties node counts to our deal SLOs and a recommended fallback (smaller quantized variant) for cost control. Attached a simple spreadsheet with our request and traffic curves (geofence-node-map-v1.xlsx).

Also cc'ing Sarah from procurement — procurement will need a rough SOW and T&Cs to start an internal approval.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood commit node-count per region + lead time?
2) What does the canary / fallback model plan look like if capacity tightens?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Jules
EdgeLabs, Head of Platform

Attachments: geofence-node-map-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 92KB)

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Jules Martin <jules@edgelabs.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pools by geofence - initial ask

Jules — thanks, got the spreadsheet. Reposting the two asks so we can be precise: node-count/lead time and fallback model plan. Adding Lauren (capacity planning) and Rishi (deal economics) to size this.

Quick clarifying Qs before we size:
- Is the 120 concurrent sessions an average across regions or per-region at peak?
- When you say "burst +30% for 4 hours/day", is that a simultaneous burst across all regions or regional spikes (i.e., US-heavy)?
- Do you require data-residency guarantees (no cross-region routing) or soft geofence with failover allowed?

Initial thought: we can provide a committed pool per region + a tri-region burst corridor, but this affects lead time (we can provision reserved nodes in ~6 weeks in US/EU, APAC ~9–10 weeks depending on procurement). Lauren — can you draft a node mapping and a short SLO->node-count mapping? Rishi — can you run the cost delta between dedicated pool + burst lanes vs a hybrid dedicated + shared fallback model?

Hiro
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Jules Martin <jules@edgelabs.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pools by geofence - initial ask

Jules / team — I put together a proposed node mapping and a short runbook in the attached SOW draft (sow-geo-pools-draft.pdf). Key points below (balances latency SLO, cost, and lead time):

Proposed committed nodes (A100S-80GB equiv) — baseline sustained +20% buffer:
- US (west): 24 nodes (baseline 20 + 4 buffer) — supports ~50 concurrent sessions sustained; local burst corridor +8 nodes (regional shared burst pool)
- EU (Frankfurt): 14 nodes (baseline 12 + 2 buffer) — supports ~30 concurrent sessions sustained; burst corridor +5 nodes
- APAC (Singapore): 10 nodes (baseline 8 + 2 buffer) — supports ~20 concurrent sessions sustained; burst corridor +4 nodes

Notes / tradeoffs:
- These counts assume warm KV cache strategies for the heavy models. If EdgeLabs is willing to accept a quantized 4-bit fallback model for non-critical traffic, we can reduce committed nodes by ~18% and use shared-hosted capacity for the remainder.
- Lead time estimates: US/EU 6–8 weeks to provision dedicated pool (hardware + routing + HSM KMS integration); APAC 9–11 weeks due to rack/partner scheduling.
- SLA lanes: committed lanes will have 99.9% availability target; burst corridor is best-effort with automated backoff (we recommend specifying p95 latency SLO only for committed lane).
- Canary plan: initial canary rollout 10% traffic to committed pools for 2 weeks, validate token-cost, latency and KV hit-rate, then ramp to full. If KV hit-rate < 75%, we recommend increasing buffer or enabling prewarm.

Action items: 
1) Jules — confirm if concurrency numbers are regional peaks or global aggregated.
2) Sarah / Procurement — if this mapping works, we can convert SOW into a commercial term sheet and draft PO milestones.
3) Rishi/Marissa — I'll need the cost worksheet and a short note on pricing tiers (committed vs committed+burst).

Thanks — Lauren
Manager, Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sow-geo-pools-draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Jules Martin <jules@edgelabs.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Cho <sarah@procureco.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pools by geofence - initial ask

Lauren — this looks good and conservative (good). Quick answers:
- 120 concurrency is global peak; regional splits are forecasted as ~US 55%, EU 30%, APAC 15% (so numbers align with your mapping).
- Burst is region-specific (mostly US-heavy during our marketing windows).
- Geofence requirement: strict residency for EU workloads (no cross-region routing), US and APAC can failover to nearby region if needed.

Procurement note (Sarah): if you can send a short SOW and an estimated commercial summary (monthly committed cost + burst surcharge + start/end milestones tied to PO), we will start internal approvals. Our preferred start date is 2026-10-15; if provisioning slips, we need to know cutoff dates for contract signing to hit that window.

If you want a short call, I can do tomorrow afternoon — otherwise proceed to a SOW+term sheet.

— Jules
EdgeLabs
